title: Honda India Two-Wheeler Sales Hit 5.43 Lakh Units in July, Eyes Premium Push
excerpt: Domestic dispatches rose 2% to 4.76 lakh units while exports surged 35%, as Honda prepares its biggest product offensive with the ADV 160, Rebel 300 and locally-built 500cc motorcycles.
body:
• Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India sold 5,42,934 two-wheelers in July 2026, a 5% year-on-year increase from 5,15,378 units in July 2025.
  • Domestic sales grew a modest 2% to 4,76,436 units, while exports surged 35% to 66,498 units on the back of strong demand from overseas markets.
  • Honda has unveiled 10 new products for India — including the ADV 160 adventure scooter, Rebel 300 cruiser and locally-manufactured 500cc motorcycles — marking its most aggressive premium expansion in years.

Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) reported total wholesale dispatches of 5,42,934 units in July 2026, a 5% year-on-year increase over 5,15,378 units shipped during the same month last year, according to figures released by the company. The numbers represent a sequential improvement from June 2026, when Honda dispatched 5,28,281 units.

Domestic sales stood at 4,76,436 units, up a modest 2% from 4,66,331 units in July 2025. The growth rate marks a deceleration from June's 20.6% year-on-year domestic surge, reflecting a high base effect as the industry moves past the demand spike triggered by the GST 2.0 reforms of late 2025. On a month-on-month basis, domestic volumes rose marginally from 4,68,956 units in June.

Exports continued to be a bright spot, climbing 35% year-on-year to 66,498 units. Honda's overseas shipments have consistently outpaced domestic growth in recent quarters, with Q1 FY27 exports rising 36% to 1,98,123 units.

Steady Volumes, Narrowing Gap With Hero

Honda remains India's second-largest two-wheeler manufacturer behind Hero MotoCorp, but the gap between the two has been narrowing. In February 2026, the difference between Hero and Honda's monthly dispatches fell to under 4,000 units. While Hero continues to lead in commuter motorcycles, Honda's strength in the scooter segment — anchored by the Activa — and its expanding premium motorcycle portfolio have kept it within striking distance.

For the full financial year ending March 2026, HMSI sold 63.69 lakh units, a 9% increase over FY2025. The company has expanded domestic production capacity to approximately 6.14 million units annually across its four manufacturing plants at Manesar, Tapukara, Narsapura and Vithalapur, with plans to scale to 7 million units by 2027.

"We have seen healthy growth momentum supported by steady underlying demand conditions and disciplined execution across the business."

— Tsutsumu Otani, President & CEO, Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India

Biggest Product Offensive in Years

Beyond the sales numbers, the real story is Honda's upcoming product blitz. The company recently showcased 10 new products for the Indian market, its most ambitious expansion in years. The lineup spans adventure scooters, cruisers and mid-displacement motorcycles — segments where Honda has historically had limited presence in India.

The ADV 160 adventure scooter, unveiled in late July, is expected to launch around September 2026 at approximately ₹1.6 lakh (ex-showroom). Powered by a 156.9cc liquid-cooled engine with E85 flex-fuel compatibility — a first for any scooter in India — it will compete directly with the Yamaha Aerox 155 and Hero Xoom 160. Features include a TFT display with Honda RoadSync, traction control, 27-litre underseat storage and an 8.1-litre fuel tank.

The Rebel 300 cruiser — powered by the same 286cc liquid-cooled engine as the CB300R — will be manufactured locally, allowing Honda to price it competitively against Royal Enfield's Meteor 350 and Classic 350. With both standard and E-Clutch variants planned, it could arrive around December 2026 at an estimated ₹2.6 lakh.

Perhaps most significant is Honda's commitment to locally manufacture the Rebel 500, powered by a 471cc parallel-twin engine. Previously sold as a CBU import at ₹5.12 lakh, local production could slash the price dramatically. The same engine platform underpins global models like the CB500 Hornet and CBR500R, raising expectations that additional 500cc motorcycles could follow for the Indian market.

Honda also unveiled the XR300 Rally and XR300L adventure motorcycles, powered by a 293.5cc oil-cooled engine, targeting the entry-level adventure segment currently dominated by the Hero XPulse. Both are expected to launch by December 2026.

What's Next

Honda's July numbers suggest the domestic two-wheeler market is settling into a steadier growth trajectory after several months of strong year-on-year gains fuelled by pent-up demand and GST reforms. The company's near-term story, however, is less about volume growth and more about its premium pivot.

With the ADV 160 expected in September and the Rebel and XR lineups slated for late 2026, Honda is positioning itself to capture segments — adventure scooters, affordable cruisers and mid-displacement motorcycles — where it has historically ceded ground to Royal Enfield, Yamaha and Hero. The success of its localisation strategy, particularly in the 300-500cc range, could reshape India's premium two-wheeler landscape heading into 2027.
